issues.description: Class constructor mismatch for SealSaloon: the problem statement UML and text declare a constructor SealSaloon(String) (saloon name) but the solution implements a no-argument constructor public SealSaloon() and the template Main also instantiates SealSaloon with no arguments. This discrepancy between the specified API (SealSaloon(String)) and the provided code (SealSaloon()) will confuse students about the required constructor signature and whether they must accept and/or store a name parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent. Preferred fix: change SealSaloon.java to declare the constructor public SealSaloon(String name) to match the UML and problem text (optionally store the name in a private final field and add a getter). Update any example usage (Main.java) to pass a name when instantiating SealSaloon. Alternatively, if the intention is to require a no-arg constructor, update the problem statement/UML to show SealSaloon() instead. Ensure the constructor signature in the template, solution, and problem statement all match.
